title: Gravitational potential energy
target: Relate height change to near-surface gravitational energy.
criteria: Use ΔU=mgΔh with the stated g.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A book is on a shelf. One group sets U = 0 at the floor; another at the shelf. Which statement is correct?
options: They can assign different U values but agree on ΔU for the same lift.
The shelf group must have negative mass.
Changing zero changes the actual gravitational force.
Only the floor can ever be a zero reference.
cpa.guide: Potential-energy zero is a convention; physical energy differences are invariant.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A model uses U = 0 at a platform. An object is 0.4 m below it. What sign is U = mgh with upward height positive?
options: Zero because height cannot be negative.
It has no sign because force is downward.
cpa.guide: Relative height is negative, so U is negative under that chosen zero.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 2.5 kg object is raised 1.6 m. Use g = 10 N/kg. What is ΔU?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg object drops from 2.2 m to 0.7 m above a reference. Use g = 10 N/kg. What is ΔU?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 3 kg object has weight 30 N and is 2 m above the chosen zero. Which is its gravitational potential energy?
cpa.guide: Weight is force; U = weight × height = 60 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A lift raises an object twice as high in the same near-surface constant-g model. What happens to its weight and potential-energy gain?
options: Weight doubles; energy gain is unchanged.
Both become zero at the top.
Both weight and energy gain double.
Weight stays the same; energy gain doubles.
cpa.guide: Weight mg is fixed here, while ΔU = mgΔh scales with height change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
